text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accusary.

- Macedonian Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski is pleased with negotiations with representatives of almost 30 political parties in Macedonia on electoral laws and possible timing of parliamentary elections.
- Macedonian official tour of China ended with visit to Shanghai. Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov described the visit as "a political impetus for economic cooperation".
- Macedonian citizens will enter Greece with Shengen visa as of October, says head of Greek liaison Alexandros Malias.

- "Athens threw a shadow over the constructive atmosphere for cooperation in the Balkans at the ministerial conference in Salonika with the promotion of a Russian-Greek initiative for a Balkan summit," the paper comments.

- Macedonia and Poland are important political and economic partners and Poland will help Macedonian integration in the European Union and NATO. Polish president expected to visit Macedonia by the end of the year.

- Macedonian government requested from German car manufacturer Volkswagen an extension of negotiations on the future of the project A3 - Macedonian national vehicle. The German producer accepted negotiations and the new round will begin on June 16. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +381 11 222 4305
